MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Service

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
Sex: Female
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood (EDTA)
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for Alport syndrome/Thin Basement Membrane Nephropathy (TBMN)

TEST DETAILS
Next-generation sequencing (NGS) to detect sequence variants and exon deletions/duplications in COL4A3, COL4A4, COL4A5, NPHS2 genes, and exon deletions/duplications in COL4A6 gene. Variant confirmation by bidirectional Sanger sequencing.

RESULTS

Gene	Transcript	Variant	Zygosity	Classification
COL4A4	NM_000092.5	c.4923C>G p.(Cys1641Trp)	Heterozygous	Likely Pathogenic

No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants detected in COL4A3, COL4A5, NPHS2, or COL4A6.

SUMMARY
Heterozygous COL4A4 c.4923C>G p.(Cys1641Trp) likely pathogenic variant detected. This novel variant results in substitution of cysteine with tryptophan at position 1641, predicted to disrupt a critical domain of the α4 chain of type IV collagen. Similar missense variants affecting cysteine residues in this region have been reported in patients with Alport syndrome (PMID: 28991257, 31980526).

The variant is absent from population databases (gnomAD v3.1.2) and multiple in silico prediction tools classify it as deleterious (SIFT: Deleterious, PolyPhen-2: Probably Damaging, CADD: 28.4). According to ACMG/AMP guidelines, this variant is classified as likely pathogenic (PM2, PM5, PP3, PP4).

CLINICAL INTERPRETATION
This result is consistent with a diagnosis of Thin Basement Membrane Nephropathy (TBMN) and carrier status for autosomal recessive Alport syndrome. Heterozygous pathogenic variants in COL4A4 typically cause TBMN, characterized by persistent microscopic hematuria and generally benign prognosis.

If Alport syndrome is suspected clinically, a second pathogenic variant may exist that was not detected by this assay. Limitations include inability to detect deep intronic variants, complex rearrangements, or variants in regulatory regions.

Carriers of COL4A4 pathogenic variants require lifelong blood pressure and proteinuria monitoring with a low threshold for ACE inhibitor therapy to prevent progression to chronic kidney disease.

FURTHER WORK
Familial variant testing is available for at-risk relatives. Genetic counseling is recommended before testing to discuss inheritance patterns, clinical implications, and reproductive risks.

TECHNICAL NOTES
Methodology: Genomic DNA extracted from peripheral blood. Target enrichment using custom capture probes followed by paired-end sequencing on Illumina platform. Minimum coverage 30x for >99% of coding regions and flanking intronic sequences (±20bp). Copy number analysis performed using read depth algorithms. Variants confirmed by bidirectional Sanger sequencing.

Limitations: This test does not detect variants in non-coding regions (except splice sites ±20bp), balanced rearrangements, or low-level mosaicism (<20%). Pseudogene interference may affect PMS2 analysis.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
